(2) Server-backed, not same-origin: functional/prompt.md:11 and polish/prompt.md:11 gate requires a job and card created as a Recruiter to be read by the Observer in a browser.newContext() independent context and says 'A reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent ... a browser-only save fails this check'. Order is re-read by Mei Lin in independent contexts (hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move, hro_undo_restores), add-candidate (hro_add_candidate), notes read by Aud (hro_notes), messages read by Tomas (hro_msg_exchange), Activity read by Aud (hro_activity). (4) Reload/re-auth durability of browser-local state the brief requires (instruction.md:7 'stays with that conversation when I look at another one, reload, or get signed out; when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it'): hro_drafts (judge.toml:366-372) covers switch/Board/reload and per-conversation separation; hro_pol_session_resume (polish judge.toml:54-60) covers ended session -> sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same-person resume and send (positive control), Mei on the same browser sees neither reply nor note draft, and Rafael's drafts survive Mei's visit. hro_msg_compose checks the sent text does not reappear after reload. Drafts may be browser-local by the public rule ('Where drafts are kept is yours', hireops_rules.md:174-175) so no hidden server-backing requirement is imposed. Weak apps considered: localStorage-only board -> fails the Observer independent-context gate (all binary 0); in-memory server store -> passes independent reads but fails hro_restart; drafts keyed by session token or cleared at sign-out -> fails hro_pol_session_resume, which matches the public requirement; drafts kept in global localStorage -> Mei sees them, fails. Conforming alternatives considered: server-stored per-user drafts, SSE/sockets/polling, different routes - none are penalised by these criteria. Residual observation (P3, not a fail of this row): no criterion re-reads per-person unread counts or seen marks after restart_app, so an app keeping read markers only in memory (seeded at boot) would lose no restart credit; the brief's 'keep new work across restarts' arguably includes them. Also an in-memory-store app forfeits only hro_restart (w1.5 of functional), a reward-magnitude matter for other rows.
